key_insight: CaBi2B2O9 ferroelectricity comes from coupled polar and octahedral distortion modes, with interlayer sliding between Bi2O2 and perovskite blocks acting as the fundamental structural driver.
engineering_relevance: This work identifies a design rule for high-temperature layered ferroelectrics with strong polarization, useful piezoelectric response, and intrinsic insulating behavior.
method: Group-theoretic mode analysis of the ferroelectric phase transition
First-principles calculations of structure, polarization, and piezoelectric response
Energetic analysis of trilinear mode coupling and insulating behavior
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the A2_1am phase is stabilized by Γ5- X2+ X3- trilinear coupling and that calculations were used to link structure, polarization, piezoelectricity, and electrical insulation in both Ta and Nb compounds.
watch_item: The mechanism is inferred from theory and symmetry analysis, so experimental confirmation of the predicted mode coupling and layer-sliding mechanism is still important.
paper_title: The origin of ferroelectricity, polarization and high resistivity in Aurivillius CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb)
